title: ArborCloud Hosted Search Rerank — Fidelity vs Cost deepwalk

Jared to send pricing tiers + hosted pilot contract template by 2027-03-10
Samira and Oliver to sync on security questionnaire answers, schedule follow-up security deep-dive week of 2027-03-15
action_items: Maya Singh - provide benchmark script and sample curl commands - 2027-03-11
Jared Collins - share hosted pilot pricing and SLA summary - 2027-03-10
Samira Patel - email SOC2 report request and KMS requirements - 2027-03-12

summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints focused on tradeoffs between relevance fidelity and per-query cost/latency. Customer interested in a short pilot and security review for production onboarding.
transcript:
[00:00] Jared Collins: Hey everyone, Jared from Redwood Inference — thanks for carving out the time. quick roll call?
[00:08] Leah Torres: Leah here - head of search at ArborCloud.
[00:11] Devon Ruiz: Devon, ML eng.
[00:13] Samira Patel: Samira, security.
[00:15] Tom Hsu: Tom, product.
[00:17] Jared Collins: Great. Maya and Oliver from my side are on as well. Quick agenda: we'll run through the hosted embeddings and reranker flow, show a couple of live queries, talk about perf/cost tradeoffs and then cover security.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Hi all, I'll start with the API shape so you can see how easily it slots into your pipeline.
[00:38] [00:38] Maya Singh: So first, call /v1/embeddings with your doc batch, we return vectors and metadata; later you call /v1/rerank with candidate list and we compute a final score. we'll demo both.
[00:50] Devon Ruiz: Quick q — do you expect us to host the vector DB or do we rely on Redwood?
[00:55] Jared Collins: Hosted model + embeddings return is just the hosted API. For vector store you can use your own or a managed vector DB like Pinecone or Algolia, but we also provide suggestions for emb maintenance. Many customers run Redwood embeddings -> their vector DB -> pass top K into rerank endpoint.
[01:12] Leah Torres: And rerank endpoint — is it scoring full doc text or embeddings? how does that pipeline look?
[01:18] Maya Singh: Good question. Typical flow: you compute embeddings, index them in your store, retrieve top N with approximate NN, then call our /v1/rerank with original query + candidate docs (we accept precomputed embeddings too). The reranker uses a cross-attention model to compute pairwise relevance and returns reordered candidates and a confidence score.
[01:40] Tom Hsu: What are typical latencies? our SLO for web queries is 200ms P95.
[01:46] Maya Singh: For hosted small rerank models P95 can be 60-120ms for N=5, larger cross-attention rerankers are more like 200-350ms depending on doc length. We have continuous batching to help throughput but for tight latency you pick a lower-capacity model or tune sequence lengths.
[02:05] Devon Ruiz: How do you balance cost — like per-query cost — vs fidelity?
[02:10] Jared Collins: Two levers: choose lighter reranker (distilled or quantized), and tune K (how many candidates you send). Also use prefix/KV caching — if you have repeated queries or long dialogs we cache key/value states for LM reranks to avoid recompute. That knocks down per-request cost significantly.
[02:30] Samira Patel: On security — do you retain embeddings or PII? our legal requires retention policy and encryption.
[02:36] Oliver Park: By default hosted API does transient retention only for debugging windows; for enterprise pilots we do configurable retention and can integrate with customer KMS for at-rest encryption. We can also offer private deployments (VPC) if required.
[02:52] Leah Torres: Can you run a pilot on hosted first then move to private? that's our preferred path.
[02:57] Jared Collins: Absolutely — our routing layer makes that seamless. Pilot hosted, then Dedicated or Private if you need stricter isolation.
[03:05] [03:05] Maya Singh: I'll pull up a quick demo — small sample dataset Leah shared earlier. Bear with me while I run a couple queries.
[03:20] [03:20] Maya Singh: Ok sending query one: "how to configure multi-region failover" — retrieving top 10 from their index then passing 5 to rerank.
[03:35] [03:35] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[03:40] [03:40] Maya Singh: Results come back — our reranker bumped doc #3 to #1 because it had the explicit step-by-step cheat sheet, confidence 0.87.
[03:52] Devon Ruiz: Interesting. On internal metrics we'd look at MAP@5 and NDCG. do you provide evaluation hooks?
[03:58] Maya Singh: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates with your eval set; you can log labels and run regression checks across model rollouts.
[04:10] Jared Collins: We also provide model diffing so when you change a reranker you can see which queries degraded.
[04:20] Tom Hsu: Pricing — ballpark for pilot of ~200k queries/month?
[04:25] Jared Collins: For hosted, ballpark we quoted in the deck — roughly $X per 1k re-ranks on a medium model plus embeddings per 1k vectors. I'll send the tiered pricing; pilots often use an experimental discount.
[04:40] Leah Torres: We have a hard constraint: 150ms median response ideally, and cost target under $0.10 per user query (including vector retrieval).
[04:50] Maya Singh: We can outline two pilot configurations: high-fidelity (better relevance, higher cost, higher latency) and low-cost (distilled reranker, lower K). We'll demo both.
[05:05] [05:05] Maya Singh: Switching to the Console — this is the per-route dashboard. you can see token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency, and an A/B rollout interface.
[05:20] [05:20] Maya Singh: here's a canary we ran — you can see a 3% drop in NDCG when moving to a quantized reranker for that dataset, so you can automate rollback.
[05:36] Samira Patel: For SOC2 and audit logs — can the console provide exportable audit trails per API key?
[05:41] Oliver Park: Yes, we keep audit logs tied to API tokens and can retain them per your retention policy. They are also available via the private s3 export if needed.
[05:55] Devon Ruiz: A couple of nitty-gritty: do you accept precomputed embeddings for rerank? and can we pass along vector distances?
[06:02] Maya Singh: Yes on precomputed embeddings — we accept vectors and perform cross-attention reranking using them. You can also include your retrieval score as a feature, we use it in reranker inputs.
[06:15] Leah Torres: What about cold-start behavior — new docs, how quickly do they show up in rerank?
[06:20] Maya Singh: The rerank call is stateless w.r.t index — as soon as your index has vectors, retrieval returns them and rerank uses what you provide. For host-managed indexing (if you used Redwood's vector tooling) we have ingestion pipelines with near-real-time indexing, usually a few seconds.
[06:35] Tom Hsu: Can you share an example API payload for rerank?
[06:38] Maya Singh: Sure, it's pretty small: query text, list of candidates with text and embeddings or doc ids, optional features like retrieval score. I'll paste sample curl in the follow-up.
[06:50] Devon Ruiz: How about throughput — we're seeing spikes to 200 qps during sales periods.
[06:55] Jared Collins: For spikes, Dedicated capacity or autoscaling policies help. Hosted has soft-bursting but Dedicated gives guaranteed GPU pools. We can also suggest batching strategies — continuous batching reduces cost at high throughput.
[07:12] [07:12] Samira Patel: On encryption — you said KMS. Do you support customer-managed keys across the hosted offering?
[07:18] Oliver Park: Yes, customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM integrations are supported on enterprise pilots and Private. For fully hosted small accounts we manage keys, but we provide attestations and options for bring-your-own-key for higher tiers.
[07:35] Leah Torres: Any instance of tokenization or PII stripping? we ingest logs and want to mask customer emails.
[07:42] Jared Collins: We have a pre-ingest filter option — you can filter or redact PII before embeddings are computed; that's configurable in the ingestion pipeline.
[07:55] [07:55] Maya Singh: Ok quick live perf test — I'll run the same N=5 rerank across three model profiles: original cross-attention, distilled, and quantized.
[08:05] [08:05] Maya Singh: Model A (full) P95 220ms, Model B (distilled) P95 90ms, Model C (quantized) P95 130ms; relevance delta: Model B -2% NDCG vs A, Model C -5% NDCG.
[08:25] Devon Ruiz: that's useful. If we can get <110ms with acceptable -2% NDCG that might be our sweet spot.
[08:31] Maya Singh: Exactly. And note we can tune K from 10 down to 3 which reduces compute but might drop recall.
[08:42] Tom Hsu: For the pilot we want to A/B three variants and measure CTR/relevance over two weeks, sound right?
[08:48] Jared Collins: Yup, and we can help set up metric logging in Redwood Optimize to track NDCG, CTR, and latency.
[09:00] [09:00] Leah Torres: On compliance timeline—Samira, do you think security sign-off can be done in two weeks?
[09:05] Samira Patel: Depends on docs. If we get SOC2 and KMS details, plus the ingestion filter config, two weeks is likely. We'll need a security deep-dive with your infra person.
[09:17] Oliver Park: I can be that infra person for the deep dive next week.
[09:22] Devon Ruiz: One more technical: can the reranker use external signals like user click counts as features?
[09:28] Maya Singh: Yes, arbitrary numeric features can be passed per candidate; we embed them into the model input and they often help rerankers.
[09:38] [09:38] Jared Collins: Let's talk success criteria for the pilot — Leah?
[09:42] Leah Torres: Increase MAP@5 by at least 8% over baseline and keep median latency under 120ms for the chosen variant. Also security sign-off. If we hit that in 2-3 weeks, risk to roll to prod.
[09:55] Tom Hsu: Budget approval requires a clear cost estimate; can you give an approximate monthly cost for the mid-tier config?
[09:59] Jared Collins: Will send numbers but mid-tier for 200k qpm (typo: I mean 200k queries/month) would likely fall into our pilot bracket pricing — I'll attach a worked example.
[10:12] Maya Singh: I'll also share a spreadsheet with cost by K and model choice so you can play with it.
[10:20] Devon Ruiz: Are there any hard limits on doc length for rerank? some docs are 6k tokens.
[10:26] Maya Singh: We support long context but costs scale. For very long docs we recommend chunking or extractive candidates, or using a hybrid approach where you pass summary + full text only when needed. We have a long-doc reranker variant as well.
[10:42] Samira Patel: For the security deep-dive, we'll want network diagrams and certs.
[10:47] Oliver Park: noted — I'll prepare network diagrams and an SSO/SAML flow doc.
[10:54] [10:54] Jared Collins: Quick poll — are you leaning hosted pilot or do you want to go straight to Dedicated?
[10:59] Leah Torres: Hosted pilot first.
[11:02] Tom Hsu: Agreed.
[11:04] Devon Ruiz: Hosted pilot but with KMS and stricter retention.
[11:08] Samira Patel: Hosted with customer-managed KMS and audit logs export.
[11:12] Maya Singh: Great — so pilot scope: 3 variants A/B test for 2 weeks, 200k queries/month slice, support for KMS + audit logs, NDCG/MAP tracking via Optimize.
[11:26] Jared Collins: Cool. I'll summarize next steps at the end. quick question from the chat — competitor feature parity w.r.t Algolia?
[11:34] Maya Singh: Algolia is strong on search infra and latency; our differentiation is model-first reranking and unified inference controls. For semantic relevance at scale you'd plug our reranker into Algolia retrieval too.
[11:50] Devon Ruiz: One last: will you provide a dedicated slack channel for the pilot?
[11:53] Oliver Park: Yes, we'll create a pilot channel and invite your team.
[12:00] [12:00] Maya Singh: Time for a rapid fire recap: action items and owners — Maya will send the benchmark script, Jared pricing, Oliver network docs, Samira initial security questions.
[12:15] Leah Torres: Sounds good. any blockers?
[12:18] Tom Hsu: none from product.
[12:20] Devon Ruiz: none.
[12:22] Samira Patel: none once docs arrive.
[12:25] Jared Collins: Great — we'll get the follow-ups in your inbox. thanks everyone.
[12:30] [12:30] End of recording.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mislabels and short crosstalk; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache in one spot). The recording length was 52 minutes; timestamps here reflect the first 12 minutes of detailed transcript excerpt and then summarized notes to align with duration.
